title: iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS
lead: Use the SwiftUI app to configure HLS or progressive MP4 sources, startup playback, bitrate, and buffering, then try source switching and live rewind. iOS and iPadOS can select the shared Web UI; tvOS uses the system UI.

blocks.text: Preparation and build

Xcode and XcodeGen 2.46.0 are required. The declared minimum OS versions are iOS 15.0 and tvOS 15.0, and the Player is pinned to 3.128.0. The Player is a binary XCFramework, so swift build alone cannot build the app. Synchronize the licenses and shared UI in the common preparation, then run the following starting at the repository root.

xcodegen version
cd apps/ios
xcodegen generate
mkdir -p Showcase.xcodeproj/project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm
cp Package.resolved Showcase.xcodeproj/project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved
open Showcase.xcodeproj

Check that xcodegen version reports 2.46.0. In Xcode, choose Showcase-iOS or Showcase-tvOS, select a destination, and run. Configure a development team and signing for a physical device. Allow com.showcase.dvr.Showcase-iOS for iOS or com.showcase.dvr.Showcase-tvOS for tvOS on the Player license.

Synchronize the shared UI before running xcodegen generate. The generated iOS target includes the WebUI JavaScript and CSS as resources. Without those files, selecting a custom mode will not show the intended UI. tvOS does not use this Web UI.

blocks.title: Unsigned iOS Simulator build from apps/ios
blocks.text:
xcodebuild -project Showcase.xcodeproj -scheme Showcase-iOS \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' \
  -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
Suggested screen workflow

items: Select Live HLS or VOD HLS under Source. The first Live HLS source loads at startup. Autoplay is off and mute is on. Start playback with the player’s play button.
On iOS or iPadOS, switch Player UI between Default, Sports, Live (DVR), and Cinema. tvOS has no such selector and uses the system UI.
After live playback starts and the rewind window becomes available, use the −10s, −30s, −60s, and −120s helper buttons. These numbers are distances from the live edge.
Use Go to live edge to return to live. Wait for the seek to complete and the LIVE display to settle.
Read mode, dvrAvailable, behindLive, atLiveEdge, and windowDuration in DVR state. Event log shows recent source loads, seeks, window-expiry events, and related activity.

blocks.text: Changing the iOS UI recreates the Player and SwiftUI view and reloads the selected source. It does not preserve playback position or playing state. Compare appearances with that reload behavior in mind. The Sports scores and player details are fictional sample data, not a sports-data service.

blocks.title: Do not add DASH to the Apple catalog
blocks.text: The Apple SDK in this configuration accepts HLS and progressive MP4. The app’s catalog contains only HLS. Loading DASH with the pinned SDK causes a precondition failure and terminates the app. Do not add it to the catalog even though SourceKind includes a DASH enum case. Use Web or Android to compare DASH behavior.
Edit source and playback configuration

items: Choose Configure source and playback below the source presets. iPhone and iPad show a sheet; tvOS opens a full-screen native form. On tvOS, move focus with the remote and press Select; text fields use the system keyboard.

Enter an absolute HTTP(S) Source URL, select HLS or Progressive MP4, and optionally enter a title and HTTP(S) poster URL. Empty title or poster values clear them. DASH and offline packages are not offered.

Set an optional start offset in seconds and choose Automatic, Start, or End. Blank offset uses the SDK default. Automatic means the beginning for VOD and the live edge for live. Signed finite offsets are accepted and the SDK corrects them to stream boundaries; live offsets apply when playback starts.

Choose Autoplay after source load, Start muted, and SDK time shift / DVR. Defaults are off, on, and on. The separate Allow DVR controls (app) switch also governs the app quick-seek buttons. Enter maximum bitrate in whole bit/s (0 = unlimited) and forward buffer in finite nonnegative seconds (0 = SDK choice).

Read Reload source or Recreate player and reload source before selecting Apply. Invalid fields show an explanation and disable Apply. Reset to applied restores only the draft; Cancel discards it. Applied settings last for the current app session.

blocks.text: Source fields and start position changes reload the source on the existing player. Playback, bitrate, and buffer changes recreate the player and native view, then reload the complete current source including title, poster, and offset options. UI mode, the app DVR switch, and event log remain in place. Apply does not preserve playback position or playing state; the configured start position and Autoplay determine the restart. Selecting a source preset replaces source-specific fields and offsets with its defaults while keeping player settings.
When something does not work

items: If the app builds but cannot play, check the Player license, allowed bundle identifier, network, and reference source. An empty Local.xcconfig used only for compilation does not provide a playback license.
When generating the project for the first time, run sync-env.sh, synchronize the shared UI, then run xcodegen generate.
If the HLS rewind buttons are disabled, start playback first. While paused, the app may continue waiting for the window to become available.
If the paused playback position falls outside the live retention window, the DvrWindowExceeded event requests a return to the live edge.
TimeChanged snapshots also check whether a live stream has ended and become VOD. This handles cases where DurationChanged alone would miss the transition.

blocks.text: Running tests and reading recorded results

The Showcase-iOS-Configuration and Showcase-tvOS-Configuration schemes run hostless tests on the exact app model/configuration sources without a Player license or shared UI resources. A clearly invalid synthetic key permits SDK object construction only. The tests cover URL/number validation, SDK field mapping, rejected/no-op Apply, source reload, and player recreation retaining source options, UI selection, and the app DVR switch. They do not establish playback or network behavior. CI runs the iOS scheme on an available iPhone simulator and keeps a generic tvOS simulator build; the tvOS unit and remote GUI results below are separate recorded checks. Replace the simulator names with installed destinations and run from apps/ios.

blocks.title: Hostless configuration tests without a license
blocks.text:
xcodebuild -project Showcase.xcodeproj -scheme Showcase-iOS-Configuration \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=<IOS_SIMULATOR_NAME>' \
  -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile -parallel-testing-enabled NO \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
xcodebuild -project Showcase.xcodeproj -scheme Showcase-tvOS-Configuration \
  -destination 'platform=tvOS Simulator,name=<TVOS_SIMULATOR_NAME>' \
  -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile -parallel-testing-enabled NO \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test

The opt-in ConfigurationUI schemes launch the real app, so they require the normal allowed Player license, network access, and reference source. An empty key is an SDK startup precondition failure. The iOS test covers invalid drafts, Reset, source metadata Apply, and mute/bitrate/buffer Apply with the source retained. The tvOS test uses remote focus and Select to edit source type and autoplay, then Reset. Screenshots are retained in the Xcode result bundle.

blocks.title: Configuration GUI checks with the app license
blocks.text:
xcodebuild -project Showcase.xcodeproj -scheme Showcase-iOS-ConfigurationUI \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=<IOS_SIMULATOR_NAME>' \
  -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile -parallel-testing-enabled NO \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
xcodebuild -project Showcase.xcodeproj -scheme Showcase-tvOS-ConfigurationUI \
  -destination 'platform=tvOS Simulator,name=<TVOS_SIMULATOR_NAME>' \
  -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile -parallel-testing-enabled NO \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test

These configuration GUI checks use the SDK default UI. They do not qualify the shared Web UI, advancing playback, start-offset accuracy, bitrate enforcement, physical devices, casting, offline playback, or Analytics receipt. The separate Showcase-iOS-Runtime scheme below checks the shared UI and playback behavior.

blocks.title: Recorded configuration checks
blocks.text: On October 20, 2026, the hostless configuration schemes passed six tests each on iOS and tvOS simulators. The GUI scheme passed one test each on iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.4, iPad Pro 11-inch (M5) / iOS 26.4, and Apple TV 4K (3rd generation) / tvOS 26.4. The retained iPhone and TV editor images were inspected. This verifies these configuration workflows in the SDK default UI; it does not add physical-device or playback qualification to the separate October 19 record.

blocks.title: Test DVR calculations from the repository root
blocks.text: swift test --package-path apps/ios/DvrKit

The optional Showcase-iOS-Runtime scheme checks the real SDK and shared UI. Replace <SIMULATOR_NAME> below with an iOS simulator name installed in your Xcode. A Player license, network access, and the reference streams are required.

blocks.title: Run from apps/ios
blocks.text:
xcodebuild -project Showcase.xcodeproj -scheme Showcase-iOS-Runtime \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=<SIMULATOR_NAME>' \
  -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile -parallel-testing-enabled NO \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test

This test uses the real SDK and model, with visible controls in the shared WebView. It checks VOD, starting playback through the UI, switching HLS sources, rewind, return to live, DVR state changes, and recreation with Cinema UI. License errors or unreachable streams are not replaced with mocks or treated as successful skips.

blocks.title: Recorded verification scope
blocks.text: The October 19, 2026 record reports one pass, zero failures, and 11.670 seconds on an iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.4 simulator, using Player 3.128.0 and shared UI 4.15.1. These are recorded results, not a new test run. They do not cover physical devices, tvOS playback, TV remotes, casting, offline playback, or Analytics receipt. Successful iOS/tvOS builds in CI are also separate from actual playback.
Applied configuration code

In Configuration, open Show applied code to read the Player, Source and UI settings already sent to the SDK. Editing the draft does not change the code until Apply. iOS provides Copy code and text selection. tvOS displays the code and has no clipboard integration in this sample. License values are omitted; the Player key is shown as a placeholder.
